summary: Simmons Peak lookout camp (1924) and L-4 tower (1933), St. Joe NF; last staffed 1972, burned by lightning in 1984; site reached by a forest road.

facts.design: L-4 cab atop a concrete base (1953), per firelookout.com; Idaho Fire Lookouts says L-4 tower
facts.status_note: Burned down from lightning in 1984; no source describes what remains at the site

staffing.status: Last staffed 1972 (Idaho Fire Lookouts); known staff Tom Boehr (1967) and Charlie Kevis (1930s)

visit.trail_note: Route guide describes a 3-mile forest road (FS 346) off Red Ives Creek Road that climbs to the former lookout; no source says whether visitors may go there

events.note: L-4 cab set atop a concrete base

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com describes an L-4 cab atop a concrete base; Idaho Fire Lookouts calls it an L-4 tower atop a concrete base; the statewide FFLA list gives a two-story cab. The story reports all three descriptions.
firelookout.com names the St. Joe National Forest for the lookout; the route guide places the road in the Idaho Panhandle National Forest. No source explains the difference, so both are stated.

notes_for_editor: Structure is described three ways across sources (see resolved_conflicts); kind two_story in the record rests on the FFLA list.
